description: Synthetic, hand-labelled prompts for testing the lab's complexity router. Labels say which tier is the cheapest one expected to meet the quality bar.

samples.prompt: What time does the Northwind support desk close on Fridays?
Which form do I use to update a borrower's mailing address?
Classify this upload as payslip, bank statement or ID: 'Statement period 01-31 March, opening balance 1,204.10'
Is the hardship hotline open on public holidays?
Tag this message as complaint, question or praise: 'The app keeps logging me out.'
How many days do we keep call recordings?
Where is the escalation matrix stored?
Classify this ticket priority: 'Customer cannot see their payment schedule.'
Draft a polite email telling a borrower their document upload was received and is under review.
Summarise this 3-page case history into five bullet points for the next agent.
Rewrite this payment reminder so it reads more warmly without changing the due date.
Explain the difference between a payment holiday and a payment plan in plain English for a customer.
Draft a reply to a customer asking why their autopay date moved.
Summarise last week's escalation notes for the team stand-up.
Turn these meeting notes into an action list with owners.
Write a short internal announcement about the new document upload portal.
Analyse these three hardship-policy drafts, compare their operational risk and recommend one with trade-offs.
Review this portfolio summary and identify segments where the arrears trend and the policy change interact.
Compare our escalation process with the proposed one and assess the impact on complaint handling times.
Assess the risk of moving document retention to a new vendor and propose controls.
Design a decision tree for routing hardship requests, including edge cases and failure modes.
Evaluate whether the proposed fee waiver rule could treat customer groups inconsistently and explain why.
What changed in the collections script between version 4 and version 5, and why might agents push back?
Check this summary of a 40-page audit report for anything it left out.
